hero.title: Enterprise blockchain architecture: decide honestly, design carefully
hero.subtitle: Learn the test that says when a ledger helps and when it does not, design permissioned and consortium networks, scale and connect them, protect data, set up governance and record decisions like a senior architect. Every task is checked and explained.

Pass each module quiz (70% or more). Short tests inside the lessons give instant feedback.
Complete the architecture document and the final assessment.

faq.q: Does the platform run Hyperledger or other networks?
faq.a: No. The labs check your analysis, designs and writing. Code listings are for you to read and run in your own environment.

faq.q: Is the course for or against blockchain?
faq.a: Neither. It teaches an honest test. A recommendation not to use blockchain is a good outcome when it is the right one.

faq.q: Is it legal or compliance advice?
faq.a: No. Data-protection and financial rules differ by country; involve qualified counsel.

activities.title: Compare three-year costs
activities.objective: Compare the total cost of a consortium blockchain with a shared database, including the savings that justify it.
activities.scenario: A blockchain costs more to build and run but avoids reconciliation work. Compare the costs over the years in B5, and find how long it takes to pay off. (Teaching figures in rupees.)
steps: In B7 work out the blockchain total: setup plus (yearly running cost minus yearly reconciliation avoided) times the years.
In B8 work out the database total in the same way (column C).
In B9 work out the difference: blockchain minus database.
In B10 show Blockchain cheaper if B9 is below zero, otherwise Database cheaper.
In B11 work out the years to break even: the extra setup cost divided by the yearly saving difference, rounded up.

checks.label: B10 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B9<0,"Blockchain cheaper","Database cheaper")

checks.label: B11 is the break-even
checks.explain: Extra setup over the yearly saving difference.

activities.title: Estimate the throughput gain
activities.objective: Estimate how many simple transfers fit on the main chain and with a rollup that publishes compressed data.
activities.scenario: A block has 30,000,000 gas and arrives every 12 seconds. A plain transfer costs 21,000 gas. A rollup transaction costs about 1,600 gas of published data. (A teaching model.)
steps: In B7 work out how many plain transfers fit in a block, rounded down.
In B8 work out the transfers per second on the main chain.
In B9 work out the rollup transactions per second: the number that fit in a block (rounded down) over the block time.
In B10 work out the improvement ratio: B9 over B8.
In B11 show Large improvement if the ratio is above 10, otherwise Modest improvement.

checks.label: B7 is the transfers per block
checks.hint: =INT(B2/B3)

checks.label: B8 is the transfers per second
B9 is the rollup rate
checks.hint: =INT(B2/B4)/B5
checks.explain: Fit in a block, then per second.

checks.label: B11 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B10>10,"Large improvement","Modest improvement")

activities.title: Set safe timelocks for an atomic swap
activities.objective: Check that the timelocks in a two-chain atomic swap leave a safe margin.
activities.scenario: Alice locks funds on chain A for 48 hours. Bob locks funds on chain B for 24 hours against the same secret. Alice reveals the secret on chain B first, so Bob needs time to use it on chain A. (A teaching model.)
steps: In B7 work out the margin between the two timelocks in hours.
In B8 show Safe margin if the margin is at least the required margin in B4, otherwise Too tight.
In B9 work out the spare time beyond the required margin.
In B10 show the worst-case lock-up for Alice in hours.
In B11 convert that lock-up to days.

checks.label: B7 is the margin
checks.explain: The longer lock minus the shorter.

checks.label: B8 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B7>=B4,"Safe margin","Too tight")

checks.label: B10 is Alice's lock-up
checks.hint: Try the formula =B2 here.
checks.explain: The long lock is her worst case.

activities.title: Score and rank project risks
activities.objective: Rank project risks by likelihood times impact and count the serious ones.
activities.scenario: A blockchain programme has five risks. Score each from 1 (low) to 5 (high) for likelihood and impact.
steps: In D2 work out the score: likelihood times impact. Fill down to D6.
In E2 show High if the score is 15 or more, Medium if it is 8 or more, otherwise Low. Fill down to E6.
In B8 count the High risks.
In B9 find the highest score.
In B10 work out the average score.

checks.label: E2 is the rating
checks.hint: =IF(D2>=15,"High",IF(D2>=8,"Medium","Low"))

checks.label: E6 is the rating
checks.hint: =IF(D6>=15,"High",IF(D6>=8,"Medium","Low"))

checks.label: B8 counts the High risks
checks.hint: =COUNTIF(E2:E6,"High")

checks.label: B9 is the highest score
checks.hint: =MAX(D2:D6)

checks.label: B10 is the average score
checks.hint: =AVERAGE(D2:D6)

activities.title: Final project: write an enterprise architecture and decision document
activities.objective: Produce a professional architecture and decision document for a real enterprise use case, including an honest test of whether blockchain is the right tool.
activities.scenario: Choose a real multi-party use case such as supply-chain tracking, trade finance, certificate verification or cross-institution records, and write the document an architecture board would review.
steps: Add a Heading 1 with the use case and 'architecture and decision document'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Business problem, Is blockchain the right tool, Architecture, Scalability, Privacy and compliance, Governance, Risks and cost, Recommendation.
Under Is blockchain the right tool compare it with at least one alternative.
Under Architecture list at least four components in bullets.
Under Risks and cost list at least four risks in bullets.
Give a clear recommendation, which may be not to use blockchain.
Keep it between 380 and 760 words.
